Resolves #21615

🌿 A planner can no longer shorten a booking below its minimum without being told why.

`examples/scheduler/eventEditor` shows a dental practice's day: five treatment rooms and 25 appointments named by treatment, six of them already at the 30-minute minimum. A double-click, or Tab to an appointment and Enter, opens the scheduler's editor through `AppointmentEditor`, a subclass that hides Progress, labels the resource field "Room" and keeps only the close tool. Save writes the record, the bar follows and the toolbar names the change. An end below the minimum is refused with the minimum in the message: the scheduler's refusal from #21722 (PR #21724), which this branch carries.

Merge order: #21724, #21727 and #21711 have merged. `dev` is merged in at `07b6cbd213`, so the diff is the example alone.

Evidence: L3 (headless Chromium e2e and frames of the example) → L3 required (AC-1 to AC-5 are rendered behaviour). Residual: none.

## Deltas from ticket
- The record's "title, room, start and end" comes from `editorConfig: {module: AppointmentEditor, title: 'Edit appointment'}`. The engine's editor has no per-field config, so the subclass hides Progress and names the resource a room.
- The hint says "Tab to it and press Enter" rather than "focus it": a click focuses the grid, not the bar, and two Tabs from the top of the page reach the first appointment.
- Drag and resize are off, so the editor is the only way to change a booking here (#21614 is the drag example).

## Test Evidence
`e2e/scheduler/EventEditor.spec.mjs` at `79b2ccaaad` (dev `07b6cbd213` merged in): 15 of 15 locally over three repeats, and green on the hosted e2e-engine shards (run 44875607106). With #21727's `e2e/timeline/EventEditor.spec.mjs` at `ee9597f05a`: 22 passed over two repeats.

The three typing arms failed on hosted runners three times (runs 44862268192, 44871160850, 44874815916) while passing locally under en-US and de-DE, UTC and Berlin, and 6x CPU throttling. The third run settled the cause: with the Title focused first (`fdaee5fa20`), so the editor had arrived, the native time input read back the record's own end twice and 00:00 once, so the typed digits never reached it. `setEnd` now fills the input (`79b2ccaaad`), as the timeline spec fills its date input. Before #21711 merged, the two focus arms failed (focus sat on the grid view), which is why #21710 blocked #21615.

Frame critique:
- Fixed after the cold read. The rule is a sentence, not a pill. The hint reads at full contrast. The day fills 1440, where it had stopped 40 px short. The body gridlines sit on the hour ticks: the default step was 120 px and the hour 141 px. The status keeps its line, so a save no longer pushes the plan down at 390.
- Fixed by #21727: the refusal reads on one line under the End row at both widths, and at 390 each time field folds under its date.
- Left to Ada's follow-up (her 4e04bc72): the invalid mark sits on the End date, not on the time that changed; the Room label sits above its select while the other labels sit left (defect-notes 42c2b3a2 and b7174c24); at 390 the labels take close to half the dialog's width.
- Engine gap, now merged as #21740: the body gridline step comes from the axis' tick, 147 px here as measured, so the example's hand-set step is gone (`87e6034ead`) and the frames show the same lines.
- Not done: the bars show no times (a 30-minute bar is 74 px wide), and the phone hint says double-click because a double-tap is unverified.

## Cold look
One cold reader of the builder's seat (Claude Sonnet, given the frames and the AC only), read before the fixes above: first frame 7 at 1440 and 5 at 390, editor 6 at 1440 and 5 at 390. It proposed two changes. The rule as plain text is taken. The refusal on the time field at full width is an EventEditor change, passed to #21727's owner.

**The graded pair (at the merged head).** Two readers without context (Claude Sonnet, fresh read-only subagents given only the eight whole-page frames, unlabelled) graded `scheduler/basic` and this example, first frame and editor at both widths, in swapped order:

| Reader | Shown first | `scheduler/basic` | This example | The biggest defect it named here |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `scheduler/basic` | 6 | 8 | on the phone fewer than two hours show, bars are cut mid-word, nothing says the plan scrolls |
| 2 | this example | 5 | 7 | the same: two hours on the phone, bars chopped at the edge, no cue that it scrolls sideways |

Both would show this example to a colleague, and both see the lower 40 % of the desktop frame empty. Their shared top defect, the phone's missing scroll cue, splits by owner. This example's share is in `ee9597f05a`: the phone hint adds "Scroll sideways for the rest of the day.", and the 390 spec checks that it shows. The plan there shows 276 of 1323 px, about 1.9 of the day's 9 hours. The engine's share, an affordance visible at rest on touch widths, is defect-note e5d91886 for the grid's owner.
